content.intro: Making HTTP Requests is lesson 151 in APIs, Networking, and Database Integration. Integration code should isolate network or database calls, use parameters instead of string-built commands, validate external data, and define transaction boundaries.
content.why_it_matters: External systems fail and return untrusted data, so integration code needs timeouts, validation, and clear data boundaries. This lesson focuses on making http requests and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for making http requests. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: HttpClient
items.text: Treat HTTP and database responses as untrusted boundaries. Set timeouts, check status codes, parameterize SQL, validate deserialized results, and make transaction scope and disposal explicit.

items.title: GET and POST requests
items.text: Treat HTTP and database responses as untrusted boundaries. Set timeouts, check status codes, parameterize SQL, validate deserialized results, and make transaction scope and disposal explicit.

items.title: Sending JSON data
items.text: Validate serialized input and version its schema where needed; successful parsing does not guarantee valid business data.

items.title: Reading responses
items.text: For reading responses, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to making http requests, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Reusing HTTP clients
items.text: Use explicit timeouts, parameterized database commands, small service boundaries, and validation for external results.

items.title: Cancellation and timeout handling
items.text: Await I/O-bound tasks, pass cancellation tokens across boundaries, and protect shared mutable state explicitly.
